Relevant Resources

  • The new Hotpatching feature is now generally available. Please see Hotpatching feature for Windows Server Azure Edition virtual machines (VMs) for more information.
  • Windows 10 and Windows 11 updates are cumulative. The monthly security release includes all security fixes for vulnerabilities that affect Windows 10 and Windows 11, in addition to non-security updates. The updates are available via the Microsoft Update Catalog. For information on lifecycle and support dates for Windows 10 and Windows 11 operating systems, please see Windows Lifecycle Facts Sheet.
  • Microsoft is improving Windows Release Notes. For more information, please see What's next for Windows release notes.
  • A list of the latest servicing stack updates for each operating system can be found in ADV990001. This list will be updated whenever a new servicing stack update is released. It is important to install the latest servicing stack update.
  • In addition to security changes for the vulnerabilities, updates include defense-in-depth updates to help improve security-related features.
  • Customers running Windows Server 2008 R2, or Windows Server 2008 need to purchase the Extended Security Update to continue receiving security updates. See 4522133 for more information.

Known Issues

You can see these in more detail from the Deployments tab by selecting Known Issues column in the Edit Columns panel.

For more information about Windows Known Issues, please see Windows message center (links to currently-supported versions of Windows are in the left pane).

HEIF Image Extensions Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in HEIF Image Extensions allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system.

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows NTFS Tampering Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Time-of-check time-of-use (toctou) race condition in Windows NTFS allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Modern Device Management (MDM) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Inadequate encryption strength in Windows Modern Device Management (MDM) allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The attacker must inject themselves into the logical network path between the target and the resource requested by the victim to read or modify network communications. This is called a machine-in-the-middle (MITM) attack.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability? An attacker in a position to modify an affected device’s MDM network traffic could provide a specially crafted signed management response. Successful exploitation could allow code to run as SYSTEM. User interaction is not required.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Azure CycleCloud Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure CycleCloud allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain ROOT privileges.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability? An authenticated attacker who controls a compute node in an affected cluster could register a specially crafted node name. If an administrator later runs the affected topology operation, successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute commands as root on the cluster controller.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Missing authorization in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The type of information that could be disclosed if an attacker successfully exploited this vulnerability is file content.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper restriction of rendered ui layers or frames in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass the Visual Studio Code Workspace Trust feature, allowing content from an untrusted workspace to run commands or code without the user first granting trust. See Workspace Trust for more information.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace. Successful exploitation could bypass Workspace Trust protections and allow attacker-controlled content to execute code in the context of the user. User interaction is required, but the user does not need to grant trust.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows CNG Key Isolation Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when the Windows Cryptography Next Generation (CNG) Key Isolation service improperly handles memory. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run processes in an elevated context.

To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would first have to gain execution on the victim system. An attacker could then run a specially crafted application to elevate privileges.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting how the Windows CNG Key Isolation Service handles memory.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can run a malicious application locally inside an AppContainer could submit specially crafted graphics data to the isolated graphics compilation service. Successful exploitation could let the attacker perform actions within the affected service's isolated security context, outside the attacker's AppContainer. No action by another user is required.

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows DHCP Server Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Exposure of sensitive system information to an unauthorized control sphere in Windows DHCP Server allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

According to the CVSS Metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability would rely upon complex memory shaping techniques to attempt an attack.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to infer limited information from memory in a privileged process by observing comparison results. It does not provide unrestricted read access to that process's memory.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is network (AV:N) and user interaction is required (UI:R). What is the target context of the remote code execution?

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Word Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Word allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Word allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Word Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Microsoft Office Word allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R). What interaction would the user have to do?

An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Windows Codecs Library allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally.

For example, when the score indicates that the Attack Vector is Local and User Interaction is Required, this could describe an exploit in which an attacker, through social engineering, convinces a victim to download and open a specially crafted file from a website which leads to a local attack on their computer.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Search Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Out-of-bounds write in Microsoft Windows Search Component allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit the Windows Search component used by Microsoft Exchange Server by sending an email containing a specially crafted attachment. Exchange automatically processes the attachment for indexing, so the recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the permissions of the affected processing service.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Excel allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted workbook in an affected version of Excel and save it in a different file format. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's privileges.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Chromium CVE-2026-118309: Incorrect reference resolution

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: ASP.NET Core Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper authentication in ASP.NET Core allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a password reset request using a specially crafted email address that is treated as equivalent to another account. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to take over the targeted account. No user interaction is required.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires the attacker to control a distinct email address that an affected application's account lookup treats as equivalent to the victim's address, while messages are delivered to a different mailbox.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Chromium CVE-2026-119260: Use after free

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Resilient File System (ReFS) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Windows Resilient File System (ReFS) allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires a memory-allocation failure during specific file operations on a writable ReFS volume.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Storage Spaces Controller Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Storage Spaces Controller allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could host a malicious server and convince a user to connect to it from an affected client. When the client processes the server's response, the attacker could execute code on the client system. User interaction is required.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Storport.sys Driver Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Out-of-bounds read in Storport.sys Driver allows an authorized attacker to disclose information with a physical attack.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

Exploiting this vulnerability could allow the disclosure of certain kernel memory content.

According to the CVSS metric, attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an administrator to have enabled a specific non-default storage platform feature on the affected system. That prior configuration cannot be enabled by an ordinary user and is outside the attacker's control.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Untrusted search path in Remote Desktop Client allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain the privileges of the user account or service account running the affected process.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could place specially crafted files on a network share and convince a user to open a Remote Desktop connection from that share with clipboard redirection enabled. When clipboard data is exchanged, successful exploitation could allow the attacker to run code with the permissions of that user. The attacker does not need an account on the affected client.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Input System Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Out-of-bounds read in Windows Input System allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can execute code in a low-privilege AppContainer could exploit this vulnerability locally to escape the sandbox and elevate privileges on the affected system. No additional user interaction is required.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker could use this vulnerability to elevate privileges from a Low Integrity Level in a contained ("sandboxed") execution environment to a Medium Integrity Level.

Please refer to AppContainer isolation and Mandatory Integrity Control for more information.

This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

An unauthenticated attacker who controls a remote MCP server could convince a user to connect Visual Studio Code to that server and click a specially crafted link in a notification. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's permissions.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper access control in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could convince a user with an active, previously authenticated Visual Studio Code web-server session to open a specially crafted link. If a vulnerable older server version remains available, successful exploitation could cause that version to run and allow the attacker to execute code with the server account's permissions.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Azure DevOps Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Weak authentication in Azure DevOps Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to prepare the target environment to improve exploit reliability.

**How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability? According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H), and some loss of integrity (I:L), and some loss of availability (A:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability? **

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gains read access to the Elasticsearch search corpus but tamper or delete only search index and not the actual source of data. This will make search functionality temporarily unavailable until indices are rebuilt.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office Excel Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Excel allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted workbook in Microsoft Excel and interact with affected workbook features. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code in the context of the signed-in user.

Successful exploitation could disclose another user's configuration information, including credentials stored in that configuration. For this vulnerability, the information is exposed through diagnostic logs on a shared computer.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Incomplete list of disallowed inputs in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an extension to be installed and run despite an administrator's extension allowlist policy. The user must be convinced to install the extension.

Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation through the extension marketplace requires the attacker to control a publishing identity that meets specific conditions. Obtaining that identity is a prerequisite beyond simply creating a malicious extension.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Incomplete list of disallowed inputs in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an untrusted workspace to apply settings that should be blocked by Visual Studio Code's Workspace Trust protections. The user must open the attacker-controlled workspace.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Acknowledgment.vuln:Name: Nguyen Van Minh Duc with Saigon Newport Corporation

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace. Successful exploitation could bypass Workspace Trust protections and allow attacker-controlled content to execute code in the context of the user. User interaction is required, but the user does not need to grant trust.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation More Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Incomplete list of disallowed inputs in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace. Successful exploitation could bypass Workspace Trust protections and allow attacker-controlled content to execute code in the context of the user. User interaction is required, but the user does not need to grant trust.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation More Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

A remote attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted extension's details page in Visual Studio Code and select a malicious link. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code in the context of the user without installing the extension. The attacker does not need privileges on the user's system.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation depends on specific conditions in the user's Visual Studio Code environment, including an already-open integrated terminal. The attacker must also rely on the user viewing the affected extension's details page in a particular platform-compatibility state.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Trust boundary violation in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace and click an attacker-controlled notification. Successful exploitation could bypass Workspace Trust protections and allow commands to run in the context of the user without the user granting trust. The attacker does not require authentication.

What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an untrusted workspace to apply settings that should be blocked by Visual Studio Code's Workspace Trust protections. The user must open the attacker-controlled workspace.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Azure Confidential Clean Rooms Tampering Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Missing authorization in Azure Confidential Clean Rooms allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering over a network.

What privileges does an attacker need to exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker must be an authenticated, registered collaborator and own an input dataset in the affected collaboration.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: PowerShell Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Insufficiently protected credentials in Microsoft PowerShell Core allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

Exploiting this vulnerability could allow the disclosure of credentials.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Acknowledgment.vuln:Name: Maksim Hayder with Iron Digital Labs LLC

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Overlay Filter Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Concurrent execution using shared resource with improper synchronization ('race condition') in Windows Overlay Filter allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

vuln:Threat.vuln:Description: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Audio Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Windows Audio Service allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows NTLM Spoofing Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in Windows NTLM allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

This vulnerability discloses a user's NTLMv2 hash to the attacker who could use this to authenticate as the user.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

External attackers could send specially crafted emails that will cause a connection from the victim to an untrusted location of attackers' control. This will leak the Net-NTLMv2 hash of the victim to the untrusted network which an attacker can then relay to another service and authenticate as the victim.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Kerberos Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Weak authentication in Windows Kerberos allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls authentication in a trusted forest could send specially crafted authentication information to the target forest. Successful exploitation could raise the integrity level of the attacker's identity to System, allowing actions otherwise blocked by integrity-level restrictions where existing resource permissions already allow access. This does not grant SYSTEM-account privileges or target-forest administrator membership.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an existing trust relationship between the attacker's forest and the target forest, together with resource permissions that already allow the attacker's identity access. The vulnerability bypasses integrity-level restrictions but does not grant otherwise absent resource access permissions.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows PowerShell Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper control of generation of code ('code injection') in Windows PowerShell allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a victim, or cause a victim-controlled automated process, to invoke Invoke-WebRequest against an attacker-controlled URL. By returning a specially crafted non-2xx HTML response, the attacker could cause Windows PowerShell to parse the response through MSHTML without displaying the security confirmation prompt, which could execute embedded script in the invoking PowerShell process.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally.

For example, when the score indicates that the Attack Vector is Local and User Interaction is Required, this could describe an exploit in which an attacker, through social engineering, convinces a victim to download and open a specially crafted file from a website which leads to a local attack on their computer.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft PowerShell Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Execution with unnecessary privileges in Windows PowerShell allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

What kind of security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass Windows Defender Application Control and PowerShell Constrained Language Mode restrictions, allowing untrusted code to run with capabilities those protections are designed to block.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authorized attacker who can execute Windows PowerShell locally under Constrained Language Mode could define and invoke a crafted workflow. Attacker-controlled workflow-definition data is inserted into a generated wrapper that runs in Full Language Mode, allowing the attacker to bypass Windows Defender Application Control and PowerShell Constrained Language Mode restrictions.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Function Discovery Resource Publication Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Windows Function Discovery Resource Publication allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker on the same network segment could send specially crafted SOAP requests to a system running the Function Discovery Resource Publication service. Exploitation depends on inducing a low-memory allocation failure and winning an asynchronous request-cleanup timing condition. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code as SYSTEM.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires the target system to be under sustained low-memory (memory pressure) conditions, which are not commonly present in normal operation. This makes the vulnerability difficult to reliably trigger, as the attacker must first induce or wait for a constrained memory state before exploitation becomes possible.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office OneNote Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office OneNote allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could provide a specially crafted OneNote file and convince a user to open it and convert its ink content to text. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the user's permissions.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The attacker must inject themselves into the logical network path between the target and the resource requested by the victim to read or modify network communications. This is called a machine-in-the-middle (MITM) attack.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could obtain the encryption keys that protect data secured by Always Encrypted with secure enclaves. With access to these keys, the attacker could read the plaintext of the protected database columns, which may contain sensitive information.

I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Xbox Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Xbox allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to an affected service over the network. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the target system. No authentication or user interaction is required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Out-of-bounds read in SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with explicit permissions could exploit the vulnerability by logging in to the SQL server and could then elevate their privileges to sysadmin.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SQL sysadmin privileges.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to chain other vulnerabilities in order to successfully gain unauthorized access to the target environment.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft SQL Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected SQL Server and submitting a specially crafted query or request that triggers a memory corruption condition, allowing the attacker to execute code on the server. Authentication is required; user interaction is not required.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Teams for Android Spoofing Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Origin validation error in Microsoft Teams for Android allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H), but lead to no loss of integrity (I:N) or availability (A:N). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The Confidentiality is set to High because an attacker who successfully exploits this vulnerability could access tokens beyond a user’s typical privilege.

The exploit results in token disclosure, however it does not affect the Integrity and Availability of the system. Thus, both of these are set as None.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: JDBC Driver for SQL Server Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper verification of cryptographic signature in JDBC Driver for SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who controls or can impersonate the SQL Server could replay a legitimate attestation response while substituting attacker-controlled key material during a client connection. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to obtain column encryption keys and access or modify protected database data.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires Always Encrypted with secure enclaves to use HGS attestation. The attacker must also control or impersonate the SQL Server connection and have access to a legitimate attestation response that can be replayed.

What could an attacker accomplish by exploiting this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to bypass secure-enclave attestation, obtain column encryption keys, decrypt protected database data, and create modified encrypted data that the client accepts as valid.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Chromium CVE-2026-76024: Memory corruption

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: This CVE was assigned by Chrome. Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) ingests Chromium, which addresses this vulnerability. Please see Google Chrome Releases for more information.

Why is this Chrome CVE included in the Security Update Guide?

The vulnerability assigned to this CVE is in Chromium Open Source Software (OSS) which is consumed by Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). It is being documented in the Security Update Guide to announce that the latest version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) is no longer vulnerable.

How can I see the version of the browser?

  1. In your Microsoft Edge browser, click on the 3 dots (...) on the very right-hand side of the window
  2. Click on Help and Feedback
  3. Click on About Microsoft Edge

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to act with the SharePoint farm service identity's administrative privileges.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permissions to add or modify content on an affected SharePoint page could store malicious script content in the page. The script could run in the security context of another user when that user views and interacts with the affected content, potentially allowing the attacker to access or modify SharePoint data available to that user.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Exposed dangerous method or function in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SQL sysadmin privileges.

Why is the attack complexity rated High?

Successful exploitation requires the affected SQL Server instance to be configured as a replication distributor. Systems without this configuration are not affected.

I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Missing authorization in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to run script in the security context of the affected SharePoint user and perform actions permitted to that user.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permissions to add or modify content on an affected SharePoint page could store malicious script content in the page. The script could run in the security context of another user when that user views and interacts with the affected content, potentially allowing the attacker to access or modify SharePoint data available to that user.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: SQL Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

I am running SQL Server on my system. What action do I need to take?

Update your relevant version of SQL Server using the applicable November 2026 security update listed below.

There are GDR and/or CU (Cumulative Update) updates offered for my version of SQL Server. How do I know which update to use?

  • First, determine your SQL Server version number. For more information, see Microsoft Knowledge Base Article 321185 - How to determine the version, edition, and update level of SQL Server and its components.
  • Second, locate the range containing your current version number in the following table. The corresponding update is the one you need to install.

Note: If your version is not represented in the table, review the applicable update's prerequisites and the support status of your SQL Server release before choosing an update. Absence from this table alone does not establish that a version is unsupported.

Update Number Title Version Apply if current product version is… This security update also includes servicing releases up through…

What are the GDR and CU update designations and how do they differ?

General Distribution Release (GDR) updates provide security and other broadly applicable critical fixes. Cumulative Updates (CUs) include accumulated fixes for the applicable SQL Server release. Use the version ranges above to select the security update for your installed servicing branch; CU+GDR updates apply to the listed CU branch, while RTM+GDR updates apply to the listed RTM/GDR branch.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Error Reporting Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Windows Error Reporting (WER) when WER handles and executes files. The vulnerability could allow elevation of privilege if an attacker can successfully exploit it.

An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could gain greater access to sensitive information and system functionality. To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker could run a specially crafted application.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by correcting the way that WER handles and executes files.

What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows eSCL Scanner Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use after free in Windows eSCL Scanner allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to an affected service over the network. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the target system. No authentication or user interaction is required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') in Windows Advanced Rasterization Platform allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can run a malicious application locally inside an AppContainer could submit specially crafted graphics data to the isolated graphics compilation service. Successful exploitation could let the attacker perform actions within the affected service's isolated security context, outside the attacker's AppContainer. No action by another user is required.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:CWE: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Windows Text Services Framework Information Disclosure Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Use of uninitialized resource in Windows Text Services Framework allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could potentially read small portions of heap memory.

According to the CVSS metric, a successful exploitation could lead to a scope change (S:C). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An exploited vulnerability can affect resources beyond the security scope managed by the security authority of the vulnerable component. In this case, the vulnerable component and the impacted component are different and managed by different security authorities.

According to the CVSS metric, attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation depends on previously used memory in the affected process remaining in a readable state. These memory conditions are not fully under the attacker's control, so an attempt may not reliably disclose information.

vuln:Vulnerability.vuln:Title: Microsoft Color Management Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

vuln:Notes.vuln:Note: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Color Management allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.
